purpose: Portrait cabinet revision based on current relic, challenge, draw components

prompts.prompt:
Create a portrait 9:16 concept-art benchmark for VIGINTI, a first-person 3D card videogame. This is a rendered gameplay proposal, not a web page. Reference image 1 establishes the red/cream/navy space casino cabinet identity ONLY; radically redesign the internal screen layout as specified and zoom in. Reference image 2 establishes the desired CHUNKY low-fidelity 3D art direction: visible pixelated texture texels, faceted bevelled low-poly meshes, worn hand-painted metal, warm orange practical light and deep petrol blue, subtle dithering, deliberately coarse raster edges. Render as a convincing actual in-engine late-2000s/indie low-poly space game, NOT photorealism, NOT a glossy product visualization. Keep screen text and card ranks especially readable despite coarse materials. Sparse restrained light bloom, no scanline wash over text.

Camera: first-person robot passenger killing time aboard a long-haul space ferry in its cheap casino. Cabinet fills 97% frame width and 96% frame height. The cabinet marquee can be cropped at top. Most of the image is the playable screen, front-facing with very slight perspective, not dramatically foreshortened. At bottom a shallow physical control ledge with small HAND SCORES utility button, one large orange STAND button, small DECK utility button. Just the tips of chunky battered robot fingers at bottom corners. Absolutely no knees, legs, lap, forearms, torso or wide environmental shot. Only tiny background slivers with a hanging amber lamp and a hint of stars, no detailed background people. A partly cropped enamel mug on the left edge and a tiny phone handset at right edge are optional only if they do not steal screen space.

SCREEN STRUCTURE top to bottom, all zones must fit and be visible:
1. compact dark header: prominent "$250" labelled CASH, smaller ROUND 3 and ANTE $50.
2. A single full-width information band divided into TWO equal wide columns (NOT three columns): named RELICS list on LEFT, named CHALLENGES list on RIGHT. Small simple objects/icons accompany names but names are always visible. Each column has generous readable line lengths; allow challenge descriptions to wrap to two lines. No icon-only medallion rails. No dealer squeezed between these two columns.
3. Under that band: separate shallow full-width DEALER area containing just two small thick 3D cards, 9 of spades and one face-down star-patterned blue card, total 9 directly underneath. Do not show fake dealer AI face.
4. Under dealer: a clearly distinguished full-width DRAW TRAY, with shallow recessed blue tray, room for THREE large card positions side by side. Label DRAW above it. This is the place new cards turn over. Distinct from dealer and player hands, with a little gap before HAND 1.
5. Lower half of screen: THREE FULL-WIDTH PLAYER HAND ROWS VERTICALLY STACKED. HAND 1 above HAND 2 above HAND 3. Each hand fans ACROSS almost the entire width of its row. Cards have physical thickness and slightly varied Z heights, all corner rank-and-suit indices visible, clean aligned row boundaries. Each row has its running blackjack total directly BELOW the card fan, labelled TOTAL. These totals are the only per-hand numbers in play. No panels, numbers, symbols, score boxes, stakes, payouts, READY labels or decorative widgets to the right of the hands. No unused right column. No horizontal three-hand arrangement.
Use simple straight horizontal separators and modest restrained gold accents. Reduce decorative outlines, curved swooshes, text clutter and fake ornaments. Space and legibility are primary. Cabinet controls are physical meshes; inside the cabinet screen the cards are dimensional virtual meshes with shadows rather than flat printed UI.

Everyday play state. RELICS left shows six lines exactly: Star Bead; Heart Button; Lucky Acorn; Faded Tag; Mini Shoe; Cozy Socks. CHALLENGES right shows three readable entries exactly: "Complete 4 rounds" with "2 / 4"; "Score 4 pairs" with "1 / 4"; "Score 6 flushes" with "2 / 6". Small slim progress bars beside/below each phrase, no giant progress rings.
DRAW TRAY: one face-down blue star card in centre, faint empty-position marks on left and right. Label below the tray "TAP TO DRAW". The tray clearly has capacity for several cards, but has one card now.
HAND 1 contains five thick cards fanned widely: 2 clubs, 3 diamonds, 4 hearts, 5 spades, 6 clubs. Total 20. HAND 2 contains 6 hearts, 6 diamonds, 7 clubs. Total 19. HAND 3 contains 10 spades, 8 hearts. Total 18. All THREE rows visible; even two-card row uses the same full-width area. The orange physical STAND button is lit.
The palette is weathered petrol blue, faded red metal, warm cream cards and orange buttons. Quiet, clean readable gameplay with tactile low-poly charm. No explanatory callouts outside the scene.

HAND 1 contains SEVEN overlapping 3D cards spread widely from left to right: A hearts, A spades, 2 hearts, 2 diamonds, 3 clubs, 4 spades, 5 diamonds. Show all SEVEN readable upper-left rank indices, total 18 directly below.

All three rows remain equally wide, each fan reaches nearly from left to right with large legible indices. No score box at right. Physical STAND is temporarily dark while cards are revealing.
